title: Maximum Total from Optimal Activation Order
summary: Given two integer arrays value and limit, both of length n, you can activate elements in any order.
statement: Given two integer arrays value and limit, both of length n, you can activate elements in any order. However, the number of active elements must always be strictly less than limit[i] for the element at index i. Activating an element at index i adds value[i] to the total activation value. After each activation, if the number of currently active elements is x, then all elements j with limit[j] less than or equal to x become permanently inactive, even if they are already active. Determine the maximum total activation value by choosing the optimal order of activations.
constraints: The arrays have equal length up to 100,000.
Activation adds a value once; limits at or below the active count then become permanently inactive.
Choose any activation order to maximize the accumulated value.
hints: Items sharing a limit compete only for that group’s available activation slots.
For every limit L, retain the L largest values in that group.
Group by limit, sort values descending, and add each group’s top min(L,size) entries.
At most L members of a limit-L group can activate before that group is eliminated, and ordering groups by their eliminations realizes all selected entries.
editorial: At most L members of a limit-L group can activate before that group is eliminated, and ordering groups by their eliminations realizes all selected entries.

tests.explanation: Activating values five, three, then eight collects all sixteen.
Only one limit-one item can activate, so choose value six.
